routes.label: Translate speed, stopping, and arrival order into graph features

question: A tortoise challenges a hare to a race. The hare eagerly agrees and quickly runs ahead, leaving the slow-moving tortoise behind. Confident that he will win, the hare stops to take a nap. Meanwhile, the tortoise walks at a slow steady pace for the entire race. The hare awakes and runs to the finish line, only to find the tortoise already there. Which of the following graphs matches the description of the race, showing the distance \(d\) traveled by the two animals over time \(t\) from start to finish?
solution:
On a distance-versus-time graph, a steady speed gives a straight line. A larger slope means a faster speed, and a horizontal segment means no movement.

The tortoise's graph must therefore be a single straight rising line. The hare's graph must rise steeply, become horizontal during the nap, then rise steeply again. Finally, at the finish-line distance, the tortoise must arrive at an earlier time, which means farther left on the time axis.

Graph \(\boxed{\text{B}}\) has all three features. Graph A has the running-and-napping pattern but puts the hare at the finish first; C and E have no horizontal nap segment, and D has no constant-speed tortoise line.
